regimens.indication: Partial-Onset Seizures in Adults 16 Years of Age and Older

refs.locator: Section 2.2 Adults 16 Years of Age and Older
refs.quote: Adults 16 Years of Age and Older Initiate treatment with a daily dose of 1000 mg/day, given as twice-daily dosing (500 mg twice daily). Additional dosing increments may be given (1000 mg/day additional every 2 weeks) to a maximum recommended daily dose of 3000 mg.

regimens.dose_text: Initiate 500 mg twice daily (1000 mg/day). Increase by 500 mg twice daily every 2 weeks to maximum 1500 mg twice daily (3000 mg/day).

regimens.indication: Myoclonic Seizures in Patients 12 Years of Age and Older with Juvenile Myoclonic Epilepsy

refs.quote: 2.3 Dosing for Myoclonic Seizures in Patients 12 Years of Age and Older with Juvenile Myoclonic Epilepsy Initiate treatment with a dose of 1000 mg/day, given as twice-daily dosing (500 mg twice daily). Increase the dosage by 1000 mg/day every 2 weeks to the recommended daily dose of 3000 mg.

regimens.dose_text: Initiate 500 mg twice daily (1000 mg/day). Increase dosage by 500 mg twice daily every 2 weeks to recommended daily dose of 1500 mg twice daily (3000 mg/day).

renal_impairment.description: KEPPRA dosing must be individualized according to the patient's renal function status based on creatinine clearance adjusted for body surface area.

refs.locator: Section 2.5 Dosage Adjustments in Adult Patients with Renal Impairment
refs.quote: In order to calculate the dose recommended for patients with renal impairment, creatinine clearance adjusted for body surface area must be calculated.
Normal | > 80 | 500 to 1,500 | Every 12 hours
Mild | 50 – 80 | 500 to 1,000 | Every 12 hours
Moderate | 30 – 50 | 250 to 750 | Every 12 hours
Severe | < 30 | 250 to 500 | Every 12 hours

hemodialysis.value: 500 to 1,000 mg every 24 hours. Following dialysis, a 250 to 500 mg supplemental dose is recommended.

refs.quote: ESRD patients using dialysis | ---- | 500 to 1,000 | Every 24 hours
Table 1: Dosing Adjustment Regimen for Adult Patients with Renal Impairment

hepatic.value: No dose adjustment is needed for patients with hepatic impairment. In patients with severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C), total body clearance was 50% that of normal subjects, but decreased renal clearance accounted for most of the decrease.

refs.quote: In patients with severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C), total body clearance was 50% that of normal subjects, but decreased renal clearance accounted for most of the decrease. No dose adjustment is needed for patients with hepatic impairment.

black_box.note: No boxed warning in FDA prescribing information

refs.quote: The precise mechanism(s) by which levetiracetam exerts its antiepileptic effect is unknown.

mg_safety.note: Not reported to exacerbate myasthenia gravis

mechanism_of_action.value: The precise mechanism(s) by which levetiracetam exerts its antiepileptic effect is unknown. A saturable and stereoselective neuronal binding site in rat brain tissue has been described for levetiracetam: the synaptic vesicle protein SV2A, thought to be involved in the regulation of vesicle exocytosis.

refs.quote: Experimental data indicate that this binding site is the synaptic vesicle protein SV2A, thought to be involved in the regulation of vesicle exocytosis.

value.instructions: KEPPRA tablets should be swallowed whole. KEPPRA tablets should not be chewed or crushed. Prescribe oral solution for patients who cannot swallow tablets or have feeding tubes.

refs.quote: KEPPRA tablets should be swallowed whole. KEPPRA tablets should not be chewed or crushed.
KEPPRA may cause somnolence and fatigue. Patients should be monitored for these signs and symptoms and advised not to drive or operate machinery
Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥ 5% more than placebo) include: Adult patients: somnolence, asthenia, infection and dizziness ( 6.1 )

pregnancy_pk.value: Physiological changes during pregnancy may affect levetiracetam concentration. Decrease in levetiracetam plasma concentrations has been observed during pregnancy. This decrease is more pronounced during the third trimester.

contraception.value: Co-administration of KEPPRA (500 mg twice daily) did not influence the pharmacokinetics of oral contraceptives.

refs.quote: KEPPRA (500 mg twice daily) did not influence the pharmacokinetics of an oral contraceptive containing 0.03 mg ethinyl estradiol and 0.15 mg levonorgestrel

lactation_summary.value: Levetiracetam is excreted in human milk. The developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding should be considered along with the mother's clinical need for KEPPRA and any potential adverse effects on the breastfed infant.

refs.quote: Levetiracetam is excreted in human milk. There are no data on the effects of KEPPRA on the breastfed infant, or the effects on milk production. The developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding should be considered along with the mother's clinical need for KEPPRA and any potential adverse effects on the breastfed infant

value.effect: Levetiracetam is not metabolized by hepatic CYP enzymes and does not inhibit or induce CYP or UGT isoenzymes, conferring very low risk of pharmacokinetic drug-drug interactions.
value.management: Standard dosing may generally be maintained when co-administered with CYP substrates or inducers.

refs.locator: Section 12.3 Pharmacokinetics - In vitro data on metabolic interactions
refs.quote: Levetiracetam and its major metabolite, at concentrations well above C max levels achieved within the therapeutic dose range, are neither inhibitors of, nor high affinity substrates for, human liver cytochrome P450 isoforms, epoxide hydrolase or UDP-glucuronidation enzymes.

value.effect: Levetiracetam does not affect valproate clearance or glucuronidation, allowing safe co-administration without pharmacokinetic dose adjustments.
value.management: Monitor clinical seizure response; no pharmacokinetic dose adjustment required.

refs.locator: Section 12.3 Pharmacokinetics - In vitro data on metabolic interactions
refs.quote: In addition, levetiracetam does not affect the in vitro glucuronidation of valproic acid.
